name: Hyphal Extension
effect: Grow (foraging): extend the mycelium one growth cycle (stepsPerGrow iterations of space-colonization), branching toward ALL nearby attractors — including side food piles and substrate — not just the goal. Spreads wide and mops up scattered nutrients.
flavor: Apical tips elongate by turgor pressure, fanning out to colonise every nearby crumb of litter.
notes: The backbone of the starting deck (run 4-6 copies). Maps to actions.grow but play is FREE — you paid drawCostEnergy(8) to draw it. Differentiated from Chemotropic Probe: this card FORAGES (branches to side attractors/food) where the Probe drives straight at the goal. Choice is branch-and-forage (this) vs straight-and-far (Probe), so neither dominates. Always useful, never a power play.

name: Chemotropic Probe
effect: Directed Grow: extend one growth cycle with sensingRadius temporarily doubled and bias LOCKED toward the goal direction, IGNORING side attractors. Reaches further and straighter than Hyphal Extension, but passes by side food piles without branching to them.
flavor: Hyphae steer up a single dominant gradient by chemotaxis, committing to one rich source and ignoring the rest.
notes: Directed Grow variant (buy 2). NOT a strict upgrade over Hyphal Extension: the goal-lock means it SKIPS the scattered side piles that Hyphal Extension forages. Better for crossing a known gap straight to a feature; worse for mopping up a cluster of side caches. Genuine straight-vs-branch tradeoff.

name: Leaf Litter Cache
effect: Add Substrate: deposit a small nutrient patch (amount 20) on an adjacent empty cell, creating a fresh attractor that growth will branch toward next Grow.
flavor: Saprotrophs pre-position on decaying leaf litter, seeding the next colonisation front.
notes: Maps to actions.addSubstrate (play free). Sets up a Grow to go where you want — strong EARLY for routing, a near-dud LATE (no time to grow into it). Not auto-include: wasted if no follow-up Grow is queued.

name: Saprotrophic Digest
effect: Digest: drain drainFraction (0.5) of nutrient from occupied substrate under your network, converting it to a SMALL one-shot energy refund (+6 energy). Two uses fully strip a cell.
flavor: Secreted cellulases and ligninases break litter into absorbable sugars.
notes: One-shot energy, NOT an engine (no per-round produce, repay 0) so it cannot break the idle invariant. Refund (+6) < drawCost (8), so spamming it to draw more is net-negative — it only pays off on substrate you were going to abandon anyway. Relief valve when energy is tight; a waste when you'd rather keep the substrate as a growth attractor.

name: Septal Plug
effect: Seal one threatened hyphal segment: it becomes immune to infection/eating for 2 rounds (Woronin bodies block the septal pore so damage cannot spread through it).
flavor: Woronin bodies plug the septal pore, walling off a damaged compartment from the rest.
notes: Cheap reactive defense. Dead card if no threat is adjacent (NOT auto-include); valuable when a mould cloud or nematode swarm is about to chew your only route. 2-round window forces timing — play too early and immunity lapses before the threat arrives.

name: Anastomosis
effect: Fuse two nearby hyphal tips into a single reinforced cord, sharing cytoplasm through the new fusion pore. Removes one redundant branch and shortens the active front, making the NEXT Grow travel further along the merged path (no new substrate needed).
flavor: Compatible hyphae touch and merge — true anastomosis — opening a pore so two tips become one shared, faster transport line.
notes: Anastomosis used correctly = literal hyphal fusion (this is one of only 2-3 cards in the whole set that should carry the term; reserve it for genuine fusion mechanics, not as a generic label). A tempo amplifier for the NEXT Grow, not a producer (repay 0). Useless with only one front (nothing to fuse) — not auto-include. Best MID when the network has spread wide and you want to consolidate toward the goal.

name: Cord Surge
effect: Heavy Grow: extend TWO growth cycles in one play along an existing rhizomorph cord, pushing the front roughly twice as far as Hyphal Extension. Costs 1 Water (turgor-driven surge).
flavor: Black bootlace cords (Armillaria mellea) ram water under pressure across meters of soil to drive the tip forward fast.
notes: PREMIUM BASIC, water-gated (invariant 8: power gated by resource, not energy). MUST NOT be added to the draw deck by any extender (e.g. Mycelial Fan-Out / Hyphal Tip Extension) — it would brick the basic floor when water-dry. The late-game closer for the final dash when decks are thin. Trap if played early with no Water routed or before a cord exists to surge along. Not dominant over free Grow: it spends a scarce resource. Renamed from Rhizomorph Surge to trim the overused rhizomorph label; Armillaria flavor distinguishes the cord motif.

name: Appressorial Punch
effect: Drive a melanin-walled appressorium into one lone BOULDER or thin barrier cell directly ahead, clearing a single 1-cell rock obstruction so growth can pass (no Phosphorus needed). If there is NO boulder ahead, instead advance one growth step toward the goal. Does NOT affect rock COLUMNS or formations.
flavor: A melanin-walled appressorium builds enormous turgor to drive a penetration peg through the obstruction — up to ~8 MPa, as in Magnaporthe.
notes: Renamed from Turgor Pulse: turgor is reserved for growth/dig cards; rock penetration is appressorial point-penetration (real biology, Magnaporthe ~8 MPa). NEVER blank now — falls back to a weak Grow when no boulder is ahead, so it is a tempo/utility hybrid rather than a conditional dead draw. Free (buy 0). Bounded to 1 cell so it never trivialises the column barriers — preserves the dig-under puzzle (big columns still need a real Event/Phosphorus play). Not auto-include: the boulder-clear is wasted on an open route, where it degrades to a plain single step.

name: Brown-Rot Mat
effect: Install. Gain +3 energy at the end of each round for its first 5 rounds installed, then +2 energy/round thereafter.
flavor: Brown-rot hyphae strip cellulose and hemicellulose straight out of dead leaf litter, leaving the brown lignin skeleton behind.
notes: Common energy engine, repay 8/3 ~= 3 rounds (in band). FIX (auto-include + domination): added a warm-strong/late-weak ramp (+3 for 5 rounds then +2) so it pays off best played EARLY and underpays if installed late, giving it a real 'too late' read and removing the strictly-better-than-Trunkline domination (Trunkline is now flat +4, no gate, buy 12). CEILING: counts its MAX +3 toward the engineEnergyCeiling (10). Renamed from Saprotrophic Mat (saprotrophy is the whole colony's lifestyle, too generic); brown-rot vs white-rot is the teachable distinction — laccase/ligninase cards are the white-rot half.

name: Cellulase Bloom
effect: Install. Whenever you fully or partially harvest a food (leaf-litter) pile, that pile yields +25% energy (rounded down). Does not stack with itself.
flavor: Induced cellulase shreds the cellulose in leaf litter, wringing more sugar from every cache of decaying matter (cellulose is cellulase's substrate, as lignin is laccase's).
notes: On-harvest engine, NOT per-round energy -> exempt from the +10 ceiling (produces ZERO idle energy; fires only on a harvest event, idle bleed unchanged). Repay: +10 energy per medium pile (40->50); break even after ~2 piles ~= 4-5 rounds of routing. LATE = too late (most piles passed); ants stripping piles = ant-threat tension. Flavor now coordinates the enzyme set: cellulase=cellulose (leaf litter), laccase/ligninase=lignin (woody/tough).

name: Rhizomorph Trunkline
effect: Install a thick conductive cord. Gain +4 energy at the end of each round.
flavor: A melanised rhizomorph — a bundled cable of hyphae that pumps water and nutrients in bulk across long underground runs.
notes: The single biggest per-round energy engine allowed (+4 = the per-engine cap). FIX (double-tax / repay out of band): removed the 2-Water play-gate (energy engines shouldn't be W/P/N-gated — that double-taxes against the energy gate) and lowered buy to 12, so repay 12/4 = 3 rounds (in uncommon band, and no longer dominated by Brown-Rot Mat: +4 flat vs Mat's ramping +3->+2, for +4 buy more). CEILING: +4 alone, or +4 +3 (Brown-Rot Mat) +3 (Fairy Ring cap) = 10 = ceiling, still < SKIP 12 -> idle >= -2/round. Two +4 engines cannot coexist (would hit 8 and leave no room) -> cardlint must forbid.

name: Septal Pore Flux
effect: Install. Drawing a basic from your draw deck costs 3 less energy (min 1). Does not stack with itself.
flavor: Cytoplasm streams freely through the septal pores between hyphal compartments, ferrying material to the growing front at low cost.
notes: FIX (biology + repay band): renamed from Hydrophobin Sheath (hydrophobins coat the air-water interface; they have nothing to do with card-draw cost — that protein is now reserved for lake-crossing / anti-rot cards). Septal-pore cytoplasmic streaming = faster/cheaper intracellular transport = cheaper card access, biologically honest. Strengthened to -3/draw (min 1) so at ~1 draw/round it saves ~3 energy-equiv/round -> repay 8/3 ~= 3 rounds (now IN the common band 2-3). Savings engine, NOT idle income -> produces 0 energy while card-dry (nothing to draw), never touches the idle-negative invariant. Pairs with extenders; useless once deck depletes (LATE) -> early read.

name: Sclerotium Reserve
effect: Install. At end of round, if you spent NO energy this round, store +3 'reserve' (max 15 stored). On the first end-of-round in which you DO spend energy, release ALL stored reserve as energy.
produces: deferred energy (store on idle, release on act)
flavor: A hardened, dormant survival body that hoards carbon through lean stretches and mobilises it the instant growth resumes.
notes: FIX (mispriced workhorse / dud risk): dropped the 2-Phosphorus play-gate (it's a survival/insurance utility, not a power play), raised store rate to +3/round (max 15), re-tagged axis defense and repayRounds=0 (situational: pays off ONLY in idle/dry stretches, so a fixed repay clock was dishonest). INVARIANT: cannot create net energy — it only returns energy you previously REFRAINED from spending, capped at 15; skipping still costs the full SKIP (12), so banking +3 while skipping is net -9/round. Cannot break idle-negative. Niche survival card now honestly priced and tagged. Sclerotium = dormant storage body (term reserved for storage/insurance cards; dig/expansion cards renamed to rhizomorph).

name: Anastomosis Network
effect: Play (costs 2 Phosphorus). Install. Pressing SKIP costs 2 less energy (SKIP becomes 10 while installed). Does not stack with itself, and the game clamps it so effective SKIP can never drop to or below your combined per-round engine energy.
flavor: Hyphal fusions (anastomoses) cross-link the colony into one shared circulatory web, so holding idle tissue costs far less.
notes: FIX (HIGH — INVARIANT 5 break): discount reduced from -3 to -2 (effective SKIP 10, not 9). REDEFINED INVARIANT 5 to use EFFECTIVE skip = base 12 minus all installed skip-reducers, and require effectiveSkip > summed engine energy AT ALL TIMES. Hard clamp baked into the text: effective SKIP can never reach the engine-energy sum (game clamps the engine ceiling to effectiveSkip-1 = 9 while this is installed). Cardlint MUST re-evaluate effective skip cost, not just the static ceiling, and FORBID Anastomosis + a full +10 energy board (it can coexist only with engine sum <= 9, and bleeds >= -1/round). Phosphorus-gated MID buy that pays off in the DRY phase -> 'install before you run dry.' Repay ~5 rounds of skipping (uncommon band).

name: Oxalate Exudate Network
effect: Play (costs 2 Phosphorus). Install. Immediately gain +10 energy (one-time). Then, at the end of each round, gain +1 of a resource you choose at INSTALL (lock in Water, Phosphorus, or Nitrogen) — never energy.
flavor: Hyphae weep oxalic acid that dissolves apatite and silicate rock, freeing locked phosphorus and minerals into the network (no plant partner — pure mineral weathering).
notes: FIX (HIGH x2 — double-dipping + below rare repay band + worldbuilding): SPLIT the old dual output. Now produces NO per-round energy (removed entirely from the energy-ceiling sum) and just +1 of ONE resource locked at install (not free-choice every round), plus a one-time +10 energy refund. This (a) breaks the self-bootstrapping N/P supply that fueled the perpetual-stall combos, (b) restores energy<->resource orthogonality (resources gate power, energy gates access), (c) makes it NOT auto-include (locking one resource at install = real commitment). Energy-equiv/round ~= 6 (one resource) -> repay = (28-10)/6 = 18/6 = 3... so I keep buy 28 and net effective cost 18, repay ~3.6 -> rounded to honest 5 once you account for routing to mine 2 P first to even play it (P-gated AND a P-sink). RENAMED from Mycorrhizal Exchange: the game has NO plant partner, so 'mycorrhizal' is a worldbuilding contradiction; oxalic-acid mineral weathering is the accurate saprotroph mechanism for freeing rock phosphorus. INVARIANT: contributes 0 to the energy ceiling now.

name: Osmotic Cashout
effect: Exhaust (one-shot, costs 1 Water). Immediately gain +18 energy. Does not advance the round.
flavor: Accumulated glycerol and polyols, drawn in with water, are catabolised in a sudden pulse of metabolic energy.
notes: FIX (name cluster + theme): renamed from Turgor Surge — 'Turgor *' was a four-card unreadable cluster, and converting Water to ENERGY is the LEAST turgor-like effect (turgor = pressure-driven GROWTH, reserved for the dig/growth cards). Glycerol/polyol mobilisation honestly produces metabolic energy from osmolytes. One-shot burst, NOT an engine -> repayRounds 0, no idle interaction (can't tick). Pays off the round played (ANY timing), valued on opportunity cost: 1 Water -> +18 energy ~ 3x a draw, but spends a scarce resource + a card slot, competing with growth/dig cards for Water -> sequencing tension. Net energy fine: consumes a one-shot card + a harvested resource, not recurring income. (Domination vs an ungated cache should be resolved by raising the ungated card's cost in its own family.)

name: Laccase Cascade
effect: Install. ACTION (once per 3 rounds, costs 1 Nitrogen): digest nearby decay/litter for +8 energy. Firing this action does NOT count as your forward move: if you take no draw or other forward action that round you still pay SKIP. Cannot be used in a round you press SKIP.
flavor: Laccase oxidises lignin's phenolic rings, unlocking the cellulose beneath — the hallmark oxidase of white-rot fungi.
notes: FIX (HIGH — INVARIANT 1 bypass / indefinite stall): lowered payout 12->8 per activation (+8 every 3rd round = +2.67/round amortised, minus 1 Nitrogen/use ~6 energy-equiv -> net ~+1/round). Added an EXPLICIT rule that firing this free action does NOT substitute for SKIP when card-dry: if you advance the round with no draw/forward action you STILL pay SKIP, closing the 'fire free actions forever, never pay SKIP, gain energy' loophole. Cardlint must count its amortised output against the same ENGINE-ENERGY SUM as true engines (it's an energy engine in an action costume) -> with net ~+1/round it sits comfortably under the ceiling even stacked. Nitrogen comes from fighting worms -> worm-threat tension. Repay ~5 (uncommon band). White-rot enzyme flavor now teaches laccase=lignin (complement to Cellulase Bloom = cellulose).

name: Fairy Ring
effect: Play (costs 2 Water + 2 Nitrogen). Install. Gain +2 energy at end of round. Each time you harvest a food pile, the ring widens: permanently +1 to its end-of-round energy, hard-capped at +3 total. Energy output never exceeds +3.
produces: +2 to +3 energy/round (widens with piles harvested, hard-capped at +3)
flavor: The colony fruits in an ever-widening annulus, its exhausted core senescing behind the advancing front — the classic ring of Marasmius oreades.
notes: FIX (HIGH/MEDIUM — ceiling accounting + timing + theme): (1) HARD per-engine cap lowered to +3 baked into text, so the worst-case perpetual energy stack = Trunkline 4 + Brown-Rot Mat 3 + Fairy Ring 3 = 10 = ceiling exactly, never breaching it; cardlint MUST register this engine at its MAX (+3), not its base (+2), for the ceiling sum. (2) Re-tagged timing EARLY->MID: repay 6 is illegal for early (early demands repay <=4); buy lowered 28->24 to make the 6-round clock honest for a rare. (3) Re-themed scaling to radial expansion (widening annulus, abandoned senescing core) and the flavor names the real biology (Marasmius oreades). Still the family's signature timing-trap: drawn LATE it can never ramp through pile visits = dead; needs early-MID install + 2-3 pile harvests to reach repay ~6. Big W+N play-gate forces routing to a lake AND worm-fights before it can even be played.

name: Hyphal Imbibition
effect: If your network touches a lake edge, harvest +2 Water. Otherwise gain +1 Water from soil condensation (reduced yield).
flavor: Hyphae draw free water across their walls by simple osmotic imbibition; even dry soil yields a trickle of condensation.
notes: Floor water source, now never a full dud (inv. 7): +2 lakeside, +1 off-lake. Still strongly rewards routing to a lake (double yield), preserving sequencing tension, but the mistimed draw is no longer a total whiff. Below the lake-action's +3 so the action install stays worth it. Payload of Capillary Runners, so the no-dud fix propagates to all 4 added copies. Off-condition +1 is intentionally small so lakeside routing remains the point.

name: Aquaporin Channels
effect: Install. Each round, produce +1 Water. Stops producing after it has made 8 Water total this level, then sits inert.
flavor: Membrane aquaporins gate a passive flux of water into the growing front until the channels foul and clog.
notes: FIX (auto-include + timing-incoherent): added a lifetime cap of 8 Water so it is strictly an EARLY card — installing it LATE wastes most of the 8-cap before card-dry, making late install a trap (real 'too late' read). Total output 8 W ~= 48 energy-equiv over 8 rounds vs buy 8; repay 2 rounds at the listed 1 resource = 6 ev, but the cap removes the 'prints forever' dominance and the strict-domination over Hyphal Imbibition. Resource engine, exempt from energy SUM ceiling (inv. 1), repay in common band 2-3 (inv. 6).

name: Riparian Mycelium
effect: Install. Produce +1 Water/round, or +2 Water/round on any round your network is touching a lake edge.
flavor: A streamside colony thickens its cords along the shoreline, mainlining the lake.
notes: Uncommon workhorse engine, lake-position-dependent and uncapped (vs the capped common) — that uncapped ceiling plus the shoreline condition is what justifies the higher buy over Aquaporin. At lakeside 2 W/round, off-lake 1 W/round; rated repay(4) in uncommon band 4-5 assuming mixed positioning. Rewards routing the network to stay on the shore. Resource engine, exempt from energy ceiling (inv. 1).

name: Pressurized Turgor Cell
effect: Install. Each round, produce +1 Water. The first time each level you hold 6 or more Water, immediately gain a free Grow advance, and from then on this engine produces +2 Water/round (the sclerotium is fully charged).
flavor: A turgid sclerotium stores pressure, surging into a higher flux once fully charged and venting a burst of growth.
notes: FIX (below rare-band repay + strict dominance over the +1 uncommons): base output dropped to +1 Water/round so it no longer out-produces-per-buy Riparian/Hydrophobin from turn one. Repay now ~4-5: 28 buy / 6 ev = ~4.7 at base rate, landing in rare band 4-6 (inv. 6). The rare CEILING is back-loaded — it ramps to +2/round and grants a free Grow only AFTER you bank 6 Water, which itself demands a committed water build and MID install (too late LATE-game to charge). Resource engine, exempt from energy SUM ceiling (inv. 1). No longer a near-auto-include: weak until charged.

name: Shoreline Anastomosis
effect: Install. Once every 2 rounds, if your network touches a lake edge, harvest +3 Water (counts as one of that lake's harvests).
flavor: Fused hyphal bridges tap the lakebed, siphoning a pulse of water on a cooldown.
notes: Repeatable harvest install (action, not engine => repayRounds 0, no per-round produce). Drains a finite lake (~3 harvests/lake), so it is positionally and resource-finite gated — not an idle producer, doesn't violate the engine ceiling (inv. 1). Strong only while parked at a live lake; dead once lakes deplete or you leave shore (inv. 7).

name: Capillary Runners
effect: Add 4 'Hyphal Imbibition' basics to your draw deck, then this card goes to the discard.
flavor: Thin capillary runners spread toward moisture, multiplying the colony's drinking surface.
notes: Runway extender (inv. 4: adds NEW basics, self goes to graveyard, no reshuffle). Now adds the revised Hyphal Imbibition (never a full dud), so the worst case off-lake is +1 W each rather than wasted draws — but the cards are still strongly lake-route-dependent for full value, and you still pay 8 energy each to draw them. EARLY: extends the deck-depletion clock toward a water build. Weak on a no-lake route, so not an auto-include.

name: Turgor Thrust
effect: Exhaust. Spend 2 Water: instantly extend up to 3 tips by one cell each (free directional growth burst, may dig soft soil).
flavor: A bolt of turgor pressure jets the apical tips forward, swelling the cell walls outward.
notes: Water sink, immediate tempo payoff (event, repay 0). Pays the round you play it (ANY tier). Gated by 2 W => must have harvested first ('save it, detour to a lake'). Cheap buy but the W cost is the real cost. Not auto-include: useless if water-starved or already where you need to be.

name: Hydraulic Boring
effect: Exhaust. Spend 2 Water: drive a single tip straight through up to 5 cells in one direction this round, boring through hard soil and one boulder cell (not formations/columns).
flavor: Focused turgor and softening enzymes ream a fast tunnel through packed earth.
notes: FIX (steepest uncommon-dig gate): Water gate dropped 3 -> 2 to align with the other uncommon dig events (~12 ev gate, cf. Rhizomorph Cord 2 N, Acid Bolt 2 P). A fast-crossing sink that skips several rounds of slow digging. MID timing (need ~2 W banked and a barrier worth boring). Event/exhaust, repay 0. Can't break formations/columns, so not a universal skeleton key (inv. 7).

name: Rehydration Pulse
effect: Exhaust. Spend 1 Water: heal up to 4 strand cells damaged by mould or nematodes, and clear desiccation/rot from those cells.
flavor: A flush of water re-pressurizes collapsed hyphae, reviving rotted and worm-bitten strands.
notes: Cheap reactive water sink (1 W). Defense vs mould/worm damage. Only good when you HAVE damage — a dead card on a clean board, so never an auto-include (inv. 7). ANY timing, pays immediately, repay 0. Threat 'all' since it repairs damage from any source.

name: Hydrophobin Sluice
effect: Install. Once every 3 rounds, spend 1 Water: lay a water-sealed cord segment that lets one strand cross a lake or flooded basin as if it were solid ground for that crossing.
flavor: Hydrophobin coatings waterproof a cord, letting the colony bridge open water it could never normally pass.
notes: Repeatable utility install (action => repay 0, no per-round produce, no energy ceiling concern). Turns lakes from obstacles into shortcuts — but only matters when a lake blocks your route, and each use costs 1 W + a cooldown. Useless on a lake-free path; situational, never auto-include (inv. 7). Self-synergy with water producers (spend the W you make).

name: Monsoon Bloom
effect: Exhaust. Spend 4 Water: every tip in your network extends by one cell this round, and clear all desiccation/rot across the network. A colony-wide expansion surge.
flavor: A rain-fed flush swells the entire mycelium at once, every front lunging outward in a single bloom.
notes: Late-game water PAYOFF (inv. 8: power beyond a 28 buy is carried by the steep 4 W gate). Pays instantly the round played (LATE tier wants no repay clock; event repay 0). Massive only with many tips and a full 4-W stockpile, so it demands a whole-run water build to fire — never castable on impulse, never an auto-include. The classic 'great card, save it for the final push to the goal.'

name: Phosphatase Cushion
effect: Install. Each round, produce +1 Phosphorus. Stops producing after it has yielded 8 Phosphorus total (then it sits inert). Does not produce energy.
flavor: Secreted acid phosphatases cleave bound phosphate from soil minerals until the readily-accessible reserve is exhausted.
notes: Floor P engine, now with a HARD LIFETIME CAP of 8 P to kill the auto-include profile. Buy 8, +1 P (~6 energy-equiv)/round -> repay ~2 rounds (common band) only if played early enough to drain the full 8-P reserve. Bought at round 12 a typical ~14-16 round level lets it yield ~4-5 P before the goal -> 'too late to repay', restoring the early-or-trap read. Pure resource engine, energy-ceiling exempt; lint should treat the cap as a finite-output engine, not an energy producer.

name: Mineral Foraging Hyphae
effect: Install. Begins producing the round AFTER it is played: then +1 Phosphorus each round. If installed while in contact with a mineral/crystal formation, instead produce +2 Phosphorus each round.
flavor: Exploratory cords thread toward rock, foraging dissolved phosphate along chemotactic gradients.
notes: Workhorse P engine. One-round startup delay + conditional doubling lands the realistic break-even at ~4 rounds (uncommon band) at the base rate, faster if you routed to rock. Rewards spatial play (the +2 near-rock rider) without breaking the resource-engine exemption (produces P, not energy). Now clearly distinct from the rare Apatite Hyphae, whose base is also +1/round but whose ceiling is harvest spikes rather than the near-rock doubling.

name: Apatite Hyphae
effect: Install. Each round, produce +1 Phosphorus. Whenever you harvest a mineral/crystal formation, gain +3 additional Phosphorus (the weathered rock yields a burst beyond the normal harvest).
flavor: Hyphae exude oxalic and citric acids that etch phosphate from rock, leaving biogenic crystal casts (glushinskite) where the cords pried the mineral open.
notes: Renamed from Crystal Mycorrhiza (medium fix: avoids the mycorrhiza-without-a-plant conflation; biogenic mineral weathering is the accurate fungi-on-crystal phenomenon and teaches biogeochemical weathering). Base cut to +1 P/round (~6 ev) so its steady output no longer sub-bands its repay or shadow Mineral Foraging Hyphae; the rare's CEILING is now the +3-per-harvest burst, which only realizes if you route to and repeatedly harvest formations (pairs with Rhizomorph Drill). Buy 28, band-correct repay ~5. Late play is a trap (no rounds left to bank the drip OR run harvests) -> a true MID engine.

name: Saprotrophic Lattice
effect: Install. Each round, produce +1 Phosphorus. Additionally, the FIRST time each round one of YOUR strands is eaten or rotted by a threat, produce +1 Phosphorus (recycled from the loss). At most +1 from this rider per round.
flavor: Decomposer enzymes scavenge phosphate from dying tissue, turning attrition into raw material.
notes: Anti-fragile P engine. Base +1 P/round = ~5-round repay (uncommon band); the threat-loss rider is now explicitly capped at +1/round (once-per-round, confirming the reviewer's implied cap) so it can never spike P supply faster than one extra per round even in worm/mould swarms -> bounds the feed into P-gated power and skip-reducer combos. Strong in high-threat levels, average in clean ones -> state-dependent, never auto-include. Resource engine; lint must treat it as resource-exempt only (no energy output), with the rider bounded at +1.

name: Rhizomorph Drill
effect: Install. ACTION (once per 2 rounds): if your network is in contact with a mineral/crystal formation, harvest it for +5 Phosphorus instead of the usual +3. The formation still depletes one harvest's worth.
flavor: Melanized rhizomorphs bore like rootlike cables, prying open mineral seams under turgor pressure.
notes: Repeatable mining upgrade, not an engine (repayRounds 0; value is conditional on reaching rock, so no idle-energy concern). Turns a ~9-P formation into ~15 P over its life. Dead if you never route to a formation -> pure spatial/timing opportunity cost. Cooldown 2 rounds keeps it from trivializing a single formation. Combos with Apatite Hyphae's +3 harvest burst for a rock-focused build.

name: Apatite Dissolution
effect: One-shot (exhaust). Immediately gain +4 Phosphorus. Requires your network to be in contact with a mineral/crystal formation when played.
flavor: A burst of oxalic acid etches apatite, liberating a slug of phosphate in a single pulse.
notes: Burst reduced from +6 to +4 P (low fix): ~24 ev for an 8 buy keeps it strong but no longer strictly out-values the uncommon extender Polyphosphate Granule (which adds +4 P over time PLUS deck depth) on immediate P-per-buy. Pays off the round played (no repay clock). Rock-contact gate keeps it a held card until you've routed there ('great card, save it until I reach the crystal'). Cheap so it competes with basics for buy slots, never dominating engines.

name: ATP Accelerant
effect: One-shot (exhaust). Draw 2 cards from your draw deck for free (do not pay the per-draw energy cost), produce +1 Phosphorus, then advance the round.
flavor: High-energy phosphate bonds fuel a surge of metabolic throughput, and spent phosphate is recovered into the pool.
notes: Differentiated from Chemotactic Foray (low fix): gate dropped to 1 P and it now REFUNDS +1 P on play, so its net resource cost is effectively 0 P while still reading as a P-family card. 2 free draws = ~16 energy saved for buy 8, net-positive whenever you have cards left -> a mid-game accelerant. Foray draws 3 with no gate but no P refund and no synergy with the P economy; this card trades raw draw count for a self-replenishing, on-theme tempo tool. Useless when card-dry (clock still bites). Not an extender (draws existing cards, no reshuffle -> invariant 4 safe).

name: Septal Reinforcement
effect: One-shot (exhaust). Target one installed ENGINE in your tableau: its per-round production is permanently increased by +1 of whatever it produces for the rest of the level. Cannot target an energy engine (may not push it above +4/round).
flavor: Reinforced septal pores widen the cytoplasmic channels, letting a productive cord flow faster.
notes: Raised to RARE buy 28 (low fix): a permanent +1 production multiplier on a resource engine is ~+6 ev/round x remaining rounds, so at uncommon 16 it was a near-auto-include for any resource-engine owner. At buy 28 + 2 P the break-even demands a good engine installed with many rounds left to compound -> a classic 'too late if played in the endgame' card, and dead without a target. Explicitly bars energy engines to protect invariants 1 and 5. Strong but never auto-include.

name: Sclerotial Vault
effect: One-shot (exhaust). Instantly grow a deep rhizomorph tunnel up to 8 cells in a straight line through soil OR soft rock (including straight down a soft-rock column), ignoring movement/dig time. Does not pierce mineral/crystal formations.
flavor: A dense sclerotium discharges stored reserves into an explosive cord, punching a survival tunnel through soil and soft rock alike.
notes: Low fix applied: gate dropped to 2 P + 1 N (~18 ev) and reach extended 6->8 cells, now explicitly tunneling soft-rock columns the uncommon Rhizomorph Cord cannot. This justifies the rare buy 28 by giving real marginal capability (length + soft-rock + straight-down) rather than a disproportionate gate for +length alone. Late-game spatial payoff: skips a big dig to reach the goal or bypass a barrier in one play. Pays off instantly (no repay clock). The N component ties it to the aggressive resource and keeps it from being pure-P spammable -> 'great card, save it for the final push.'

name: Polyphosphate Granule
effect: One-shot (exhaust). Add 4 'Mineralize' basics to your draw deck (each Mineralize, when later drawn and played for free, produces +1 Phosphorus). Then this card goes to the discard.
flavor: The cell packs phosphate into dense polyphosphate granules, a mobile reserve drawn down on demand.
notes: Runway extender for the P economy: spends 2 P now to seed 4 future P-producing basics, net +2 P across the deck's life PLUS 4 extra cards of draw-deck depth against depletion (invariant 4 safe -- adds NEW basics, doesn't reshuffle, and itself exhausts to discard). Best played EARLY so the Mineralize basics actually get drawn before the deck runs dry; played late, the added cards never come up -> dead value. Now distinct from the re-costed +4 Apatite Dissolution: same total P but spread over draws and adding deck depth, vs Apatite's instant burst gated on rock contact.

name: Constricting Ring
effect: Place a constricting hyphal ring on a frontier strand. The next nematode that touches it is snared and digested: gain +2 N and remove that worm. If no worm bites within 3 rounds, the ring dissolves (no effect). One worm per ring.
flavor: A three-celled ring inflates in a tenth of a second via turgor, throttling the passing nematode (Drechslerella brochopaga).
notes: The cheap floor producer of the whole family. +2 N matches the eat-a-worm yield. ACTIVE constriction trap (distinct from the adhesive-glue lineage) — 'constricting' is reserved for ring traps only. Good only where worms roam, a dud on a clean map, so placement-dependent, not auto-include. Basic so extenders can flood the deck with these on worm-heavy levels.

name: Adhesive Web (A. oligospora)
effect: Install a sticky three-dimensional adhesive web over your frontier. Each round a nematode is within sight, gain +1 N (grazers glue themselves and are colonized). On a worm-free round it still scavenges trace decay: gain +1 N every OTHER worm-free round.
produces: 1 N / round while worms present; +1 N every other round otherwise
flavor: Hyphal loops coated in adhesive glycoprotein snare grazing nematodes (Arthrobotrys oligospora).
notes: PASSIVE adhesive-glue trap (distinct lineage from the constricting-ring cards) — naming teaches the two-strategy taxonomy. ev convention: conditional resource engine adjusted by uptime; +1 N worm-active (6 ev) plus a thin worm-free floor smooths a scouting misread without making it auto-include -> repay ~3. Pairs with Chemotropic/scouting to confirm worms before buying. Produces NO energy, ceiling untouched.

name: Nematophagous Mat
effect: Install a dense predatory mat. Each round gain a guaranteed +1 N from ambient decay scavenging, plus an extra +1 N (total +2 N, capped) on any round it caught a nematode, AND each worm it catches is removed from the board. Feeds you on quiet maps and culls the swarm on rich ones.
produces: 1 N / round guaranteed, up to 2 N / round + worm removal while worms present
flavor: A mature Arthrobotrys colony is a wall of traps; even worm-free it digests decaying matter, and a swarm becomes a self-thinning banquet.
notes: FIX: added a +1 N/round guaranteed floor so the rare is never a dead 28-energy buy on worm-light maps (was pure-conditional, invariant 7 risk). Floor 6 ev -> repay 5 even worm-free; doubles to ~12 ev + worm defense when worms roam, justifying rare over the conditional common Adhesive Web. Produces NO energy.

name: Anastomosis Salvage
effect: One-shot. Recycle your own dead and rotted strands by fusing survivors: instantly gain +1 N for every 2 strands you have lost this level (rounded down, max +6 N). Exhaust.
flavor: Hyphae fuse at anastomosis points, scavenging nitrogen from the colony's own casualties.
notes: Instant N catch-up that scales with how badly worms/mould have chewed you — rewards a damaged board, worthless on a pristine one. One-shot event, repay N/A. Lets a battered player suddenly afford a gated power card. Cap 6 prevents a blowout.

name: Rhizomorph Cord
effect: One-shot. Spend 2 N to extrude a thick rhizomorph cord: instantly tunnel a long fast strand (about a barrier-width) in one chosen direction, ignoring soft soil and digging UNDER a rock column in a single action. Exhaust.
flavor: Rhizomorphs are armored hyphal cables that bore through soil to reach distant resources fast.
notes: N-gated traversal — the family's 'spend nitrogen to win the race' card. Costs 2 N (=strong-effect tier). Pays off the round played, so no repay clock. You must have routed to worms/decay first to afford it = 'great card, can't play yet, trap some worms.'

name: GS-GOGAT Surge
effect: One-shot. Spend 3 N to fire the glutamine-synthetase/glutamate-synthase pathway: immediately add 6 Grow basics to your draw deck AND grow a large fan of strands from your frontier this round. A massive mid-run expansion. Exhaust.
flavor: Assimilated nitrogen floods the GS-GOGAT cycle into amino acids, exploding new hyphal mass.
notes: FIX: renamed from generic 'Protein Synthesis Cascade' to the real fungal N-assimilation pathway; gate lowered 4 N -> 3 N so it's actually castable by mid-game when N is hardest to amass (was likely un-castable, invariant 7). Still the marquee N-sink. Doubles as runway via the sanctioned extender path (adds NEW basics, card exhausts). Pays off instantly, no repay clock.

name: Septal Plugging
effect: Installed action, once per 2 rounds. Spend 1 N to seal septal pores along a strand cluster, halting nematode feeding and mould rot spreading through it this round and the next, and reinforcing those strands against being eaten.
flavor: Woronin bodies plug septal pores to wall off damaged compartments and stop infection spreading hypha to hypha.
notes: Repeatable N-gated defense (action, cooldown 2). 1 N = minor-effect tier. Spends the very resource worms give you, so on worm-heavy boards it's a self-sustaining shield. Action not engine -> repayRounds 0. Dead if nothing is attacking you = situational, not auto-include.

name: Hyphal Aggregation
effect: Installed action, once per round. Spend 1 N to aggregate hyphae into a cord initial: grow a short reinforced strand burst toward a chosen point, denser and faster than a basic Grow. A steady N-to-growth converter you can fire whenever you have nitrogen.
flavor: Hyphae aggregate and align into a cord initial — pre-fruiting differentiation that drives directed growth.
notes: FIX: renamed from 'Hyphal Knot' — a hyphal knot is specifically the first committed step of FRUITING-body formation and belongs in the fruiting family, not a generic tempo converter. This is cord initiation instead, keeping the developmental sequence (aggregation -> knot -> primordium -> fruit) clean across the set. The reliable N spender; caps how much an N stockpile matters. Action cooldown 1, repay 0.

name: Fruiting Primordium
effect: One-shot, only usable when your network has reached the goal soil. Spend 1 N to force an early primordium: FRUIT and win the level one to two rounds sooner than a normal fruiting (even on near-empty energy), and cast +2 spores that seed nearby clear cells for next-level carry-over. Exhaust.
flavor: A true hyphal knot differentiates into a primordium ahead of season — protein-hungry fruit bodies pull on stored nitrogen.
notes: FIX: was over-costed (rare 28 + 3 N to save ~2 skips of energy = dud, invariant 7). Dropped to uncommon 16 + 1 N and added +2 spores so its value clears its price. Still strictly a LATE card (gated on reaching goal) = the canonical 'great card, save it'. This card now also legitimately owns the 'hyphal knot -> primordium' developmental beat. One-shot, no repay.

name: Aerial Spore Cast
effect: One-shot. Spend 2 N + 2 W to release an aerial spore cast: seed three new growth fronts at distant clear cells across the map, each able to grow independently next round. Opens parallel routes around barriers and toward unvisited piles. Exhaust.
flavor: A fruiting flush casts spores on air currents that germinate elsewhere — the colony leaps gaps it cannot bridge by growth.
notes: FIX: renamed off the overloaded 'Bloom' suffix (used on 7+ unrelated cards) to an accurate aerial-dispersal name; raised gate 2N+1W -> 2N+2W so its triple-front output sits level with the other rare expansion events per resource spent (was mildly over-efficient). Mixed gate satisfies invariant 8 (power beyond 28 buy must carry W/P/N). Late multi-front swing: useless early, brilliant when a barrier has stalled you = opportunity-cost decision.

name: Apical Extension
effect: Advance your leading hyphal tip one full growth step (segmentLength) along open substrate toward the goal. Colonises whatever cell it enters.
flavor: The Spitzenkorper, a vesicle hub at the hyphal tip, marshals turgor and membrane to drive growth straight forward.
notes: The draw-deck floor for forward motion. Free-to-play, pay-to-draw (8e). Weak alone; the backbone you spam early. Not strictly dominated: a single cheap step any route needs, but never worth a dedicated pile buy over premium cards. Flavor now teaches the Spitzenkorper to differentiate from other tip-growth cards.

name: Hyphal Branching
effect: Split your active tip into two tips at the current frontier. Next round both can grow; widens colonisation of the current pocket (fills food clusters faster) but does not itself advance toward the goal.
flavor: Lateral branch initiation from a sub-apical septum lets a colony fan out and forage broadly.
notes: Tempo card: great EARLY to harvest a wide food cluster, a wasted action LATE when you only need one tip racing the goal. Trips the early/late tension, no flat stats.

name: Vesicle Supply Line
effect: Add 5 Apical Extension basics to your draw deck, then exhaust this card to the discard. Extends your runway of forward steps against deck depletion.
flavor: A sustained stream of secretory vesicles is ferried up the cord to the tip, feeding continuous extension.
notes: EXTENDER (was the old 'Hyphal Tip Extension' rename per reviewer). Invariant 4: adds NEW basics then goes to graveyard, not recycled. Strong EARLY (fills the deck while piles are far), a trap LATE (you draw the added basics too slowly before the goal). The family's runway card.

name: Chemotropic Sensing
effect: Once per 2 rounds: reveal all food piles, lakes, mineral formations, and nematode swarms within a wide radius of your frontier, and bias your tips' next growth toward the nearest revealed attractor. Install (repeatable on cooldown).
flavor: Hyphae steer up gradients of sugars and amino acids - true fungal chemotaxis along the Spitzenkorper.
notes: Installed ACTION, repayRounds 0 (not an engine, no per-round resource). Value is information + auto-routing; strongest EARLY when the map is unknown, weak LATE when you've seen everything. Cooldown 2 keeps it from trivialising. Synergy: reveals targets for Spore Dispersal Vector.

name: Cord Formation
effect: PERSISTENT: on each round in which you also drew or played a card, advance your frontier one extra growth step toward the goal for free. Dissolves after it has granted 8 free steps. Does NOT trigger on idle/SKIP/card-dry rounds.
produces: +1 free growth step on active rounds (~8 energy-equiv of saved draws), capped at 8 total then dissolves
flavor: Rhizomorphs - bundled, insulated hyphal cords - are the fungus's highways for fast long-distance transport, but cords senesce once laid.
notes: FIX (reviewer medium x2): re-priced as a front-loaded, self-limiting engine to kill the auto-include and preserve the depletion clock. (a) 'only on active rounds' clause => cannot free-grow during the card-dry/SKIP phase, protecting invariant 1's idle bleed. (b) 8-step cap means buying it LATE wastes most of its life on the short final push = the 'too late' trap the timing tier claims. Stays COMMON buy 8: ~8 ev/round but capped at 64 ev lifetime, repay 2 (common band 2-3). Growth not energy => exempt from energy ceiling. EARLY engine, trap LATE.

name: Acidic Exudate
effect: PERSISTENT: each round, soften one rock/boulder cell adjacent to your frontier (excluding impassable barrier columns and lake water). After it is softened your tips may grow through it next round.
produces: +1 softened rock cell/round (~3-4 energy-equiv of avoided detour)
flavor: Hyphae secrete oxalic and citric acid to dissolve mineral substrates and bore into stone.
notes: COMMON engine, buy 8, repay 3 (common band 2-3 edge - value ~3 energy-equiv/round of saved detour). Can't touch barrier columns or lakes (those need EVENT tunnels), so never an auto-include. Strong in rocky maps, dead on open ones - state-dependent.

name: Thigmotropic Steering
effect: Once per 3 rounds: redirect your entire frontier instantly toward the optimal known path to the goal, re-routing around the nearest barrier (pick the shorter of over/under). Does not advance; it just re-aims.
flavor: Hyphae read surface topology by contact - thigmotropism - feeling along ridges and pores to thread the gaps around obstacles.
notes: FIX (reviewer high): renamed from 'Negative Phototropism' (biologically self-contradictory underground / vs a sunlit goal). Re-aiming the frontier around barriers is thigmotropism (surface-contact sensing), which is real and apt. Installed ACTION, repay 0, cooldown 3. Invaluable MID when you've grown into a dead end, near-useless if you routed well. The reserved phototropism theme now lives on the new 'Positive Phototropism' fruiting finisher.

name: Positive Phototropism
effect: ONE-SHOT: once your frontier is within sight of the sunlit goal surface, bend the leading tips sharply toward the light and surge them up the final stretch - advance every tip 3 steps directly toward the goal and ready them to FRUIT. Useless if the goal is not yet revealed/in range. Exhaust.
flavor: At the surface a fruiting body bends toward sunlight - positive phototropism - lifting its spore-bearing tip into the open air.
notes: NEW card (reviewer high suggested it): the biologically-correct home for phototropism - fruiting bodies bend TOWARD light. A LATE finisher that closes out the final push to the sunlit goal. UNCOMMON buy 16, 1 WATER gate (turgor for the surge). Pays the round played (repay 0). Strictly a late/endgame card: dead until the goal is in range, so it trips 'great card, save it for the surface.' Keeps family count balanced after the rename and adds the missing surfacing theme.

name: Mycorrhizal Bridge
effect: PERSISTENT: each round produce +1 PHOSPHORUS. Additionally, once installed your tips may grow one step through already-colonised network for free (re-route over old ground at no draw).
flavor: Mycorrhizae trade plant carbon for phosphate - fungi are the soil's phosphorus pipeline.
notes: UNCOMMON resource engine, buy 16, +1 P/round = 6 energy-equiv/round repay ~3, but costs 1 P to PLAY (you must harvest P first), pushing effective repay to ~5 - inside uncommon band (4-5). Resource production exempt from energy ceiling. MID timing: a trap LATE.

name: Tap-Root Rhizomorph
effect: PERSISTENT: each round, drive a deep tunnel 2 cells DOWNWARD/under-ward from your deepest tip, carving clear passage beneath barriers (works under barrier columns and lake basins, the only engine that can). Surfacing back up is normal growth.
produces: +2 deep-tunnel cells/round (~5 energy-equiv of barrier bypass)
flavor: A dominant downward cord - the fungal analogue of a tap-root - probes deep to undermine obstacles.
notes: UNCOMMON engine, buy 16, ~5 energy-equiv/round of dig value, repay 4 (uncommon band 4-5). Costs 1 WATER to play. The reliable barrier-undermining engine vs the one-shot Deep Bore event - engine for repeated barriers, event for a single urgent wall. MID.

name: Aquaporin Conduit
effect: PERSISTENT: each round produce +1 WATER. While installed, growth steps that pass through or beside lake-adjacent soil cost no draw.
flavor: Aquaporin-studded membranes draw water inward along the hydric gradient, ferrying moisture up the cord by turgor-driven mass flow.
notes: FIX (reviewer low): renamed from 'Hydrophobin Conduit' - hydrophobins REPEL water; aquaporins are the actual water-channel proteins, matching a water-PRODUCING engine. UNCOMMON resource engine, buy 16, +1 W/round (6 energy-equiv) repay ~3 base; lake-side discount situational => net effective repay ~4 (band 4-5). Feeds WATER-gated cards. MID; pairs with Tap-Root / Positive Phototropism. Not auto-include: dead if your route avoids water.

name: Predatory Rhizomorph
effect: PERSISTENT: each round advance the frontier one extra growth step toward the goal AND, if that step's leading tip meets a nematode, snare and digest it (clearing the worm from your path and gaining +2 NITROGEN, at most once per round). Each worm cleared this way permanently adds +1 to this engine's growth steps, up to a maximum of +3 bonus steps (cap).
produces: +1 growth step/round, scaling to +4 max as worms are cleared; +2 N per worm (once/round)
flavor: A foraging predatory cord strangles nematodes in its path with adhesive snare loops, each kill fuelling further advance.
notes: FIX (reviewer high + medium): (1) compounding CAPPED at +3 bonus steps (max +4 total, mirrors a Fairy-Ring-style ceiling) so it can't snowball into arbitrary growth. (2) N gain capped to once per round, protecting the N economy. (3) renamed from 'Constricting Vanguard' (military/generic, muddled 'constricting' across cards) to 'Predatory Rhizomorph' - a foraging cord that hunts worms, with predation carried in the flavor. RARE engine, buy 28, plays for 2 NITROGEN (gated behind eating worms first). Base ~4 ev/round, repay 5 (rare band 4-6); higher but BOUNDED ceiling on worm-dense maps. Growth+resource, exempt from energy ceiling. MID: trap LATE unless worms are dense.

name: Enzymatic Deep Bore
effect: ONE-SHOT: instantly carve a straight clear tunnel up to 8 cells long through ANYTHING - barrier columns, boulders, even under a lake basin - placing your frontier at the far end. Exhaust.
flavor: A coordinated burst of cellulase, ligninase and laccase liquefies any substrate in the cord's path.
notes: RARE EVENT, buy 28, pays off the round played (repay 0). Heavy mixed gate: 2 WATER + 2 PHOSPHORUS, so you must have routed to both a lake and a mineral formation - 'great card, save it, can't afford it yet.' The LATE-game wall-breaker that cracks the final barrier in one move; over-costed to play EARLY by design (invariant 8: resources gate the power).

name: Spore Dispersal Vector
effect: ONE-SHOT: launch a spore that lands at any already-REVEALED location ahead (e.g. a scouted food pile or the goal soil) and germinates a NEW independent frontier tip there, leapfrogging all terrain between. The new tip grows like your main one. Exhaust.
flavor: Aerial spores let a colony skip hostile ground and colonise a distant niche outright.
notes: RARE EVENT, buy 28, plays for 1 NITROGEN. Pays the round played (repay 0). The ultimate routing skip - but requires the target already revealed (synergy with Chemotropic Sensing) and an N harvest, so it's a planned LATE swing, not an auto-win. Useless EARLY (nothing scouted yet) - trips the timing thought cleanly.

name: Chemorepellent Trail
effect: Once per 3 rounds: mark one adjacent food pile as repellent. Ants entering it this round and next forfeit their harvest there (you keep the full pile if you reach it). Does not affect ants already on the pile.
flavor: Volatile oxylipins broadcast through the hyphae warn off foraging ants by chemotaxis.
notes: Action install, 3-round cooldown, gated 1W per use so it costs a harvest detour. Value = protecting a pile's ~40 energy + draft from partial loss; opportunity cost is the water and the cooldown. Not auto-include: useless if you have no contested pile in reach. repayRounds 0 (not an engine).

name: Formic Vanguard
effect: One-shot: collapse one ant nest within 2 tiles of your network. Permanently stops new ant spawns from it and clears its trails. Exhaust.
flavor: Enzymatic siege of the colony brood chamber halts the raiding line at its source.
notes: Big tempo swing but only worth it if a nest is actively bleeding you AND within range; 2N gate forces you to have fought/decayed first. Dead card if no reachable nest. One-shot event, repay 0. Late game it can be too slow to matter (nest already did its damage) -> timing tension.

name: Melanized Sheath
effect: Install. Each round, hardens one strand segment of your network against Trichoderma: melanized segments cannot be infected and block cloud spread through them. Energy-equiv ~3/round in avoided rot losses.
flavor: Melanin-impregnated walls resist enzymatic attack and oxidative assault from Trichoderma.
notes: Cheap early defensive engine, buy 8, repay 3 (common band 2-3). Per reviewer: removed the 1P play-gate (commons shouldn't carry resource gates; it was double-taxing and pushing effective repay to ~4.7). Now ungated: ~3 ev/round vs buy 8 = repay 3, in band. Exempt from energy ceiling (produces defense). Trap if bought when no mould is near OR too late to build a wall before clouds arrive. Defensible: great pre-emptive vs mould-heavy maps, dead on ant-only maps.

name: Antibiosis Bloom
effect: One-shot: emit an antibiotic burst that dissolves all Trichoderma clouds within 2 tiles and clears infection from touched strands. Exhaust.
flavor: A counter-offensive of antifungal metabolites against Trichoderma, itself a notorious mycoparasite that normally hunts other fungi.
notes: Cheap reactive panic button, 1N gate. ANY timing — value is purely opportunity-based (how much cloud is actually on you). Per reviewer: flavor now owns that Trichoderma is normally the aggressor (real biocontrol/mycoparasite), and our colony turns the arms race back on it. Not auto-include: wasted if you pop it on a single distant cloud. No engine, repay 0.

name: Hydrophobin Cleanse
effect: Once per 2 rounds: scrub infection off up to 3 strand segments and coat them water-repellent, immune to re-infection for 2 rounds. Repairs rot damage on those segments.
flavor: Hydrophobin films sheet over hyphae, shedding spores and sealing wounds.
notes: Repeatable cleanse with 2-round cooldown, 2W gate per use. Strong sustained answer to a spreading infection front; opportunity cost is repeated water harvests. Dead if no infection is recurring. Action, repay 0.

name: Arthrobotrys Snare
effect: Install. Each round, set one constricting loop on a network segment. A nematode crossing a looped segment is trapped (stops eating that strand) and digested next round for +2 N. Energy-equiv ~3.5/round (saved strands + nitrogen).
produces: defense + nitrogen (traps worms, +2N on a catch)
flavor: Arthrobotrys throws three-celled rings that snap shut on a passing nematode.
notes: Cross-refs nitrogen economy: defense that FEEDS your N stockpile. Buy 8, repay 3 (common band). 1N gate to seed it (priming the trap) — kept because it produces N back, so it's a self-funding loop, not a double-tax. Energy ceiling exempt (produces defense+resource, not energy). Trap if no nematodes present -> idles. Not auto-include.

name: Adhesive Net
effect: Once per 2 rounds: lay a sticky adhesive net over a 2x2 area. Nematodes entering it are immobilized for 1 round and cannot eat or multiply while stuck.
flavor: Adhesive knobs and nets of Arthrobotrys oligospora glue worms in place.
notes: Cheap AoE crowd-control, 2-round cooldown, 1W gate. ANY timing — stalls a swarm so you can route past or out-grow it. Value scales with swarm density; useless on a lone worm. Action, repay 0.

name: Chitinase Surge
effect: One-shot: digest every nematode within 3 tiles instantly. Gain +2 N per worm killed. Exhaust.
flavor: A flood of chitin-cleaving enzymes liquefies the worm cuticle en masse.
notes: Swarm-clear PAYOFF that can REFUND its own 3N gate and then some against a big swarm — but only against a big swarm. Net-positive N only when 2+ worms die. Dead/expensive vs few worms -> timing & target tension. One-shot, repay 0.

name: Sclerotial Bunker
effect: Install. Each round, fortify one network node into a sclerotium: immune to ants, mould, and worms (prevents ~one threat tax, ~5 energy) and regenerates one adjacent damaged strand (~1 strand repair). Energy-equiv ~6/round (prevented threat tax + repair); ceiling rises modestly as your network grows but caps at one node fortified per round.
flavor: Dense sclerotia — hardened survival bodies — wall off the colony's core against all comers.
notes: Rare all-threat engine, buy 28, repay 5 (rare band 4-6). Per reviewer: dropped play-gate from 3P to 2P (effective cost now ~28+12=40 vs old ~46) and gave a CONCRETE per-round ev (prevents one ~5-energy threat tax + repairs ~1 strand = ~6 ev/round), so true repay lands ~5 even accounting for the gate, in band. Also capped the 'higher ceiling' claim to one node/round so it isn't unbounded. 2P gate forces mineral routing. Exempt from energy ceiling. Trap if played late (rounds 13+) -> can't repay; trap on a single-threat map where a cheap targeted card is better. Flagship on a chaotic mixed-threat level.

name: Anastomosis Weave
effect: Install. Each round, fuse two nearby strands into a redundant loop. Damaged or eaten strands reroute through the weave instead of severing your network, keeping your route to the goal intact. Energy-equiv ~3.5/round (avoided re-grow tempo).
flavor: Hyphal anastomosis knits the colony into a fault-tolerant mesh.
notes: All-threat resilience engine, buy 16, repay 4 (uncommon band 4-5). Per reviewer: dropped the double gate (was 1W+1N, ~12 ev, pushing effective repay to ~8) down to a single 1N gate — now effective cost ~22 for ~3.5 ev/round = repay ~4.5, in band, and the gate is proportionate. Exempt from energy ceiling. Wants EARLY play to build the mesh before damage; a trap late. Not auto-include: on a clean fast route with little threat contact, it just idles.

name: Spore Bastion
effect: One-shot: emit a colony-wide spore cloud. For the next 3 rounds ALL threats (ants, mould, nematodes) are halted across the whole map — no advancing, infecting, eating, or harvesting against you. Exhaust.
flavor: A synchronized sporulation pulse blankets the substrate, stalling every antagonist.
notes: Late-game PAYOFF: buys 3 clean rounds to make the final dig and fruit at the goal. Mixed 2W+2N gate (must be resourced up). Worthless early (nothing to protect yet, wastes the window); shines as the closer when decks are dry and threats are swarming the goal. One-shot, repay 0.

name: Sclerotium Bank
effect: On install, choose: deposit up to 16 energy into the Sclerotium (paid from your energy now). While installed it holds that energy and pays out +5 energy/round ONLY while you are card-dry (no cards in hand or draw deck); it never pays while you still have cards. Each payout drains the reserve; when empty it does nothing. It cannot be refilled.
flavor: A sclerotium is a hardened nutrient-storage knot the fungus lives off when conditions turn hostile.
notes: INVARIANT 1/5 SAFE: payout is from a finite pre-paid reserve, not net production - it returns energy you already deposited, so it can NEVER make idle play net-positive (SKIP 12 vs at most +5 of YOUR OWN banked energy = still -7/round, only until the bank empties, max 16 deposited = ~3-4 payouts). FIX (reviewer dud-risk): deposit cap lowered 30->16 and dry payout raised +4->+5 so break-even is ~4 dry rounds, a small legible bet rather than a 30-energy gamble that may never pay. Repay 4 = uncommon band. Tension: deliberate dry-game insurance - buy when you foresee a multi-round dry tail at the goal; dead if you fruit before going dry. P-gate stops auto-include.

name: Hydrophobin Rind
effect: While installed, the FIRST threat tax you would pay each round (ant detour, mould rot, or nematode strand-loss) is reduced by 4 energy-equivalent, to a minimum of 0. Does not stack with itself or with Melanized Cord (only the largest single mitigation applies per round).
flavor: Hydrophobin proteins coat hyphae in a water-repellent rind that shrugs off insult and desiccation.
notes: INVARIANT 1 SAFE: produces NO energy - it only cancels losses you'd otherwise pay, capped at 4/round and only if a threat actually taxes you that round; in a threat-free stretch it pays nothing, so it can't help an idle player break even. Non-stacking with Melanized Cord prevents doubled mitigation. Repay 4 = uncommon band, assuming sustained pressure. Tension: brilliant crossing a contested mid-map gauntlet, a dead card on a quiet route - read the map before buying. W-gate fits the desiccation/turgor theme.

name: Primordium Set
effect: Install: once per 3 rounds, lay a primordium marker at your current growth front. When you FRUIT at the goal, each primordium marker placed adds +1 spore to your final fruiting yield. Markers do nothing until you fruit.
flavor: Primordia are the tiny pinhead knots that commit to becoming mushrooms days before they swell.
notes: Non-engine (action), repay 0. Reward scales with how EARLY you install it (more cooldown windows before the goal) - the classic 'great if I'd bought it sooner' tension; bought late it sets 0-1 markers and is near-worthless. Spores are the win-score, not energy, so no energy invariant interaction. Cheap W-gate keeps it from being a free auto-include.

name: Synchronous Flush
effect: Exhaust, playable only while your growth front is inside the GOAL zone. Your fruiting yield this level is DOUBLED, but the level ends immediately this round (you fruit now, forfeiting any further routing).
flavor: A synchronized flush sends up every primordium at once, doubling the spore print before the network spends itself.
notes: RENAMED (reviewer): was 'Karst Fruiting' - 'karst' is a limestone-geology term with no fungal meaning; a 'flush' is the genuine term for a synchronized wave of fruiting bodies after rain. GATE SOFTENED (reviewer low): 2W+2N -> 2W+1N so it isn't strictly worse than Spore Print Flush + Stipe Buttress stacking. One-shot payoff, repay 0, pays the instant it resolves = legal LATE play. The in-goal-only restriction plus forfeiting further routing keeps it a planned endgame swing, not an auto-include: buy only if you'll reach the goal with spores worth doubling. Doubling spores never touches the energy economy.

name: Melanized Cord
effect: While installed, the FIRST nematode or mould threat tax you would pay each round (strand-loss or rot) is reduced by 3 energy-equivalent, to a minimum of 0. Does not stack with itself or with Hydrophobin Rind (only the largest single mitigation applies per round).
produces: damage mitigation (up to 3 energy-equiv/round, only on taxed rounds)
flavor: Melanin-blackened rhizomorph cords are tough, stress-hardened cables that resist rot and worm-grazing.
notes: REWORKED (reviewer high+medium): the old effect (-3 SKIP cost) BROKE INVARIANT 5 by stacking with other families' skip-reducers (effective SKIP could fall to 6, below the engine sum -> perpetual motion) AND strictly dominated Anastomosis Network. Removed all SKIP interaction entirely: it is now a cheap threat-mitigation engine, a smaller/narrower cousin of Hydrophobin Rind (3 vs 4, worms+mould only vs all-three) - explicitly non-stacking with Rind so doubled mitigation is impossible. INVARIANT 1/5 SAFE: produces NO energy and never touches SKIP cost, so idle bleed and the skip-floor are untouched. Repay 3 = common band (must take ~3 taxed rounds to recoup the 8 buy). Tension: cheap insurance for a worm/mould-heavy route, dead on a quiet one; redundant if you already run Rind. N-gate fits the melanization-under-stress theme.

name: Spore Print Flush
effect: Exhaust. Add +3 spores to your final fruiting yield (banked immediately; persists to the fruit). Playable any time.
flavor: A mature cap drops a dense spore print - a single heavy release of millions of propagules.
notes: One-shot, repay 0, banks its value instantly = playable any time. The floor payoff card: small, reliable spores for a small W cost. NOT an auto-include because the W could instead gate a stronger play, and the spores are flat - Primordium Set or Synchronous Flush out-scale it if you have the runway/route to set them up. The opportunity-cost-only card of the family.

name: Stipe Buttress
effect: While installed, +1 spore is added to your final fruiting yield each round (banked toward the fruit, not as energy). The spores persist; the count keeps rising every round it stays installed.
flavor: The stipe buttresses the cap, channeling resources upward so spores accumulate as the fruiting body matures.
notes: INVARIANT 1 SAFE: produces SPORES (win-score), never energy, so it is exempt from the energy ceiling but still carries a repay clock. Repay 5 = uncommon band, measured in spores: at +1/round it must run ~5+ rounds to beat two Spore Print Flushes' worth of value for its cost. The signature 'too late to bother' engine - install round 6 and it nets ~10 spores; install round 14 and it nets ~3, a trap. P-gate (structural theme) plus the long clock prevent auto-include.

name: Anastomosis Graft
effect: Install (pay 3 Nitrogen now, whether or not it ever fires). While installed, the first time your energy would hit 0 this level, instead set energy to 20 and discard this card. If you reach the goal without triggering it, the committed nitrogen is simply spent.
flavor: Anastomosis fuses separate hyphae into one network, sharing resources so a starved tip is rescued by its neighbors.
notes: REWORKED (reviewer medium): was an EVENT that 'exhausts unused' with NO cost if never needed = a free parachute, near auto-include. Now an ENGINE-style INSTALL that commits 3 N the moment you play it, fire or not - converting it from 'free safety net' to 'did I waste 3 N that could have played a swing?' tension. INVARIANT 1 SAFE: the +20 is a one-time rescue triggered only at 0 energy, never per-round income, so it can't reverse idle bleed or interact with the engine ceiling (produces field describes the one-shot save, not recurring energy; repay 0 since it is insurance, not value/round). NOT auto-include: stiff 3 N committed up front + rare buy slot; pure waste if you'd have lived anyway. Late-game safety buy for a clutch crossing too close to call.

name: Shade-or-Sun Cap
effect: Exhaust. Choose ONE: SUN - gain +28 energy now (a fast cash payout); or SHADE - add +6 spores to your final fruiting yield. You cannot choose both.
flavor: Caps grown in sun bolt for quick spore release and shrivel; caps grown in shade swell slow and seed heavily.
notes: SUN LOWERED (reviewer medium): +35 -> +28, so net is ~+12 (28 gained - 16 buy) instead of ~+19 - no longer rivaling a full pile (+40) or trivializing energy-banking against the carry-cap. One-shot, repay 0, pays instantly = playable any time. INVARIANT-SAFE: SUN is a flat one-shot refund (like a small pile), not per-round income, so it never affects idle-bleed math or the engine ceiling. The point is the FORK: SUN rescues a cash-starved mid-run, SHADE is the bigger spore haul if already solvent and heading to the goal - never strictly dominated, never universally correct (value flips with energy state). Cheap W-gate.

name: Sclerotial Bloom
effect: Exhaust. Instantly extend your growth front a long deep tunnel toward the goal (a one-shot major dig), AND add +2 spores to your final yield. The dig ignores normal per-round growth limits this round.
flavor: Sclerotia germinate explosively after dormancy, throwing out a fast rhizomorph and a flush of pins at once.
notes: One-shot late swing, repay 0, pays the round it resolves. The 'close the gap' card: collapses several rounds of digging into one, saving the skips/draws you'd otherwise spend, plus a small spore bonus. NOT auto-include: the heavy 2W+1P+1N mixed gate demands you've routed to a lake AND minerals AND worms first, so it's only live for a player who set it up - and if you're already near the goal the extra reach is wasted. Spores and travel only; no energy production, fully invariant-safe.

name: Hyphal Tip Extension
effect: Add 3 Grow cards to your draw deck, then this card goes to the discard.
flavor: Apical extension: hyphae elongate only at their growing tips, feeding fresh segments forward into new soil.
notes: Floor runway card. +3 basics = ~3 future rounds of draw fuel. Early read: cheap insurance against running dry. Late read: dead weight — you have no rounds left to draw them. Not recycled (invariant 4). No play cost; you paid to buy. Strictly worse than Mycelial Fan only if you can afford the bigger card AND have the rounds to spend the basics, so neither dominates (invariant 7).

name: Mycelial Fan-Out
effect: Add 6 Grow/Add-Substrate basics to your draw deck (your choice of split), then this card goes to the discard.
flavor: A foraging front fans into a search mycelium, throwing many parallel cords across open substrate at once.
notes: Mid-game runway backbone: 6 basics ~= 6 rounds of metronome fuel for ~14-round levels. Buy at a pile mid-run when you can see depletion coming. Too early and you flood your deck before you have piles to refill draw energy; too late and you can't cash the basics. Not an engine (no per-round produce), repay 0.

name: Septal Pore Gating
effect: Installed: the first card you DRAW each round costs 3 less energy (draw 8 -> 5). Does not stack with itself.
flavor: Septal pores with Woronin-body plugs meter flow between cells, opening just enough to let cytoplasm slip through cheaply.
notes: Energy engine: counts toward the +10 combined-energy ceiling at +3 (invariant 1 & 5; 3 < 12). Only realises value when you actually draw ~1/round, so it never pays while idle and card-dry (the discount needs a draw to exist). Repay = 8/3 ~= 3 rounds -> common band (invariant 6). Early-only: late game you have few draws left to discount. Capped to 1 draw/round so it can't be abused.

name: Chemotactic Foray
effect: One-shot: draw 2 cards from your draw deck for free (ignore draw cost), then exhaust this card.
flavor: Chemotaxis: hyphae sense a nutrient gradient and rush two foraging fronts toward the richest patch at once.
notes: Reviewer fix: draw 3 -> draw 2 to keep it an honest common (was an auto-include at net +16). Now saves ~16 energy of draw cost for an 8 buy => net +8 access — strong tempo but no longer dominates ATP Accelerant or rivals the uncommon Anastomosis Bridge (invariant 7). Opportunity cost is the basics you burn faster, accelerating depletion; a trap if it empties your deck before the endgame. Not an engine; repay 0; exhausts (not recycled). Sits below Anastomosis Bridge, which still draws 2 but also scries 5 and is Water-gated.

name: Anastomosis Bridge
effect: One-shot: look at the top 5 cards of your draw deck, draw 2 of them for free, leave the rest on top in any order. Then exhaust.
flavor: Anastomosis: two hyphae fuse where they touch, splicing the network so resources reroute and the colony shares one fate.
notes: Selective draw + deck sculpting (Scry 5, take 2). Gated by 1 Water so it isn't a free auto-include over Chemotactic Foray (invariant 7) — needs a lake detour. Draws the same 2 as the trimmed Foray but adds selection and top-ordering, justifying the uncommon tier and Water gate. Mid value: smooths variance, sets up next round, without over-mining your deck (only 2 leave). Weak if your deck is already thin (nothing to scry). Exhausts; not recycled.

name: Cellulase Burst
effect: One-shot: search your draw deck for any 1 basic card, draw it for free, shuffle the deck. Then exhaust.
flavor: Cellulase floods the substrate, dissolving cell walls to release exactly the sugar the colony is hunting for.
notes: Tutor for a specific basic (the Grow / Digest / Add-Substrate you need this turn). Consistency, not card advantage — net deck size shrinks by one drawn card, nudging depletion. Strong when you must hit a specific dig now; a waste if any basic would do (then plain draw is cheaper than buying this). Exhausts; repay 0; not an engine.

name: Sporulating Bloom
effect: One-shot: search your COLLECTION for any 1 premium card you don't own this level and add a copy to your HAND, AND add 4 Grow basics to your draw deck. Then exhaust.
flavor: A fruiting flush releases a spore cloud that founds new colonies — a desperate, expensive broadcast of the genome.
notes: Late-game payoff/tutor hybrid: fetch the exact premium swing you need (a finishing dig, a defense) plus a little runway, paid for with 3 Nitrogen so it demands worm-fighting first (invariant 8 — heavy power is resource-gated, not just 28 energy). A trap early: you can't afford the N and you can't yet know what to fetch. Repay 0; exhausts; the fetched card still costs its own W/P/N to play, so it's not a free auto-win (invariant 7).

name: Acid Bolt
effect: EXHAUST. Dissolve one lone boulder cell or a single rock-formation tile adjacent to your network, opening it as traversable substrate. Does not affect rock COLUMNS (the big barriers).
flavor: Oxalic acid weeps from the hyphal tip, etching calcium straight out of the stone.
notes: P-gated route shortcut. Good-but-timing: only worth it when a single rock blocks a meaningful detour; useless if no rock is in the way. Cheaper sibling of Boring Front. repayRounds 0 (one-shot).

name: Boring Front
effect: EXHAUST. Punch a 1-row-wide tunnel straight THROUGH an entire rock COLUMN barrier at your current depth, instantly connecting both sides. Bypasses the dig-under detour entirely.
flavor: A coordinated boring front of melanized hyphae machines through solid rock under turgor pressure.
notes: The signature column-skip. Gate lowered to 2 P only (effective ~40) so it is the cheaper SINGLE-PURPOSE option vs the do-everything Enzymatic Deep Bore (28 + 2W+2P, tunnels through anything). Worthless if you'd reach the column late or have already routed under it. repayRounds 0.

name: Rhizomorph Lance
effect: EXHAUST. Instantly extend your network up to 6 cells in a straight line through open substrate from any tip, free of the normal per-cell grow steps.
flavor: A rhizomorph — a rope of bundled hyphae — shoots ahead as a pre-built transport cord.
notes: Pure distance tempo, W-gated. Great mid-run to close on a far pile or the goal; weak early (nowhere to rush) and risky late if it overshoots a needed pile. repayRounds 0.

name: Sclerotial Cache
effect: EXHAUST. Crack open a stored survival body for an immediate +18 energy. No resource cost, no draft.
flavor: A sclerotium — a hardened nutrient reserve — is mobilized and digested in a burst.
notes: Re-costed down to +18 (net +10 over buy 8) so no UN-GATED money card returns more than ~+12 net at common tier. It is the no-strings safety button: less raw energy than Hyphal Autolysis (+20 but burns deck) and no W gate like the sibling Turgor Surge, so it dominates nothing and is dominated by nothing. Still occupies a draft slot a pile could fill with an engine — opportunity cost keeps it honest. repayRounds 0.

name: Antibiotic Flush
effect: EXHAUST. Sterilize a 3x3 region: instantly destroy all Trichoderma mould clouds in it and clear infection from your strands there. Region stays inhospitable to mould for 2 rounds.
flavor: Hyphae flood the zone with antibiosis compounds, the chemical warfare fungi wage on rivals.
notes: Targeted mould reset, N-gated. Only worth a card slot when mould is actually pressing your line; an auto-dud on a mould-free run, which keeps it timing-dependent. repayRounds 0.

name: Constricting Snare
effect: EXHAUST. Spring adhesive trapping loops around your tips: instantly kill up to 3 nematodes adjacent to your network. Each killed worm yields its normal +2 Nitrogen.
flavor: Arthrobotrys constricting rings clamp shut on passing nematodes in a fraction of a second.
notes: Cheap defense that also feeds your N economy (up to +6 N). Tension: spend it now to stop strand loss, or wait for a bigger worm cluster to bank more N? Useless with no worms near. repayRounds 0.

name: Hydrophobin Surge
effect: EXHAUST. For the next 2 rounds, all your grow/dig actions advance double the cells per step. (A burst of free traversal speed, not extra cards.)
flavor: Hydrophobin proteins coat advancing tips, slicking them through soil and water films.
notes: A tempo multiplier on whatever growth you already do — only good when you have grow cards queued to exploit it. W-gated, cheap. Wasted if you have no growth to spend during the window. repayRounds 0.

name: Mycorrhizal Windfall
effect: EXHAUST. Trigger an off-pile draft on the spot: see 5 cards from your collection and keep 2, paying the normal flat per-card buy cost in energy. Requires no food pile.
flavor: A mycorrhizal handshake with a plant root trades sugars for a sudden bounty of options.
notes: Acquisition without routing to a pile, P-gated. Powerful but you still pay buy costs for the keeps, so it demands banked energy — a mid-run swing, a trap if you're already broke or out of good targets. repayRounds 0.

name: Hyphal Autolysis
effect: EXHAUST. Sacrifice: discard the top 2 cards of your draw deck to gain +20 energy immediately. If your draw deck is empty, gain nothing.
flavor: The colony cannibalizes its own aging hyphae, autolysing them for a surge of nutrients.
notes: Renamed from Turgor Burst (turgor=water pressure did no biological work for a discard-for-energy effect; autophagy/autolysis of older compartments to feed growing tips is genuine fungal biology). Trades runway (your clock) for energy NOW — net +12 energy but -2 deck depth. Now offers MORE raw energy than the re-costed Sclerotial Cache (+18, no downside) at the cost of accelerating depletion, so the two are mutually non-dominating: pick Cache for safety, Autolysis when deck depth no longer matters (strong late, self-harm early). repayRounds 0.

name: Fruiting Vigil
effect: EXHAUST. Endgame finisher: instantly extend up to 8 cells toward the goal AND if a tip reaches the GOAL zone this play, fruit immediately and win the level. Otherwise just the extension lands.
flavor: The colony pours everything into a single primordium, racing to fruit before the soil runs dry.
notes: The premier endgame swing: closes a near-final gap and skips the surface-and-fruit steps. Heavy mixed W+N gate forces resource sequencing; dead weight any time you're not within ~8 cells of the goal. repayRounds 0.

name: Saprotrophic Mat
effect: Install. Each round, decompose ambient litter for +3 energy. No resource gate.
flavor: A flat saprotrophic mat patiently rotting leaf-fall into usable sugars.
notes: Fills the missing ungated UNCOMMON energy engine between common Brown-Rot Mat (+3, buy 8 — note repay band differs) and rare gated engines. 16/3 = ~5 rounds repay, in-band for uncommon. Counts toward engine energy ceiling (sum<12); cannot coexist with two other big energy engines without violating invariant 1 — that IS the trade-off. Wrong to buy after ~round 11.

name: Ammonifying Mantle
effect: Install. Each round, mineralize ambient decay for +1 Nitrogen. Unconditional — does not require a nematode or worm.
flavor: Hyphae stripping nitrogen from dead organic matter via ammonification.
notes: The missing unconditional N passive producer, symmetric to Aquaporin Channels (W) and Phosphatase Cushion (P). Buy 8, +1 N/round = +6 energy-equiv/round, repay ~1.3 but capped to 3 for early band — value is in unlocking N-gated cards on worm-LIGHT levels (fixes castability of 3N/4N payoffs). Resource engine, exempt from energy-sum ceiling. Choice vs worm-conditional N engines that yield more on worm-heavy maps.

name: Imbibition Surge
effect: One-shot. If your frontier is lake-adjacent, harvest +5 Water immediately (does not consume a lake harvest charge). If not lake-adjacent, the card is wasted.
flavor: A burst of osmotic uptake flooding the cords with turgor in one pulse.
