notes: Cheap one-shot WATER burst mirroring Apatite Dissolution (P). Hyphal Imbibition basic only gives +2 W; this +5 fills the burst-access gap so all three resources have a cheap burst. The lake-adjacency requirement is the timing tension (positional, not auto-include). Single-lake maps (lakeCountMax=1) make routing matter.

name: Mineral Etch
effect: If your frontier is touching a mineral/crystal formation, harvest +2 Phosphorus (does not consume a formation charge). Otherwise wasted.
flavor: Acidic exudate etching phosphate loose from apatite at the contact face.
notes: Cheap repeatable basic P harvest, direct mirror of Hyphal Imbibition (W basic, +2). Phosphorus had only engines + the Apatite Dissolution event; this is the draw-deck floor card for P. Added to deck by Polyphosphate Granule extender or drafted as a basic. Positional gate keeps it from being a free auto-include.

name: Picket Hyphae
effect: Install. Each round, contest the nearest food pile adjacent to your frontier: ants harvest it 50% slower this round, so you reach more of its energy and draft. Produces no energy itself.
flavor: A standing picket line of fans physically crowding ants off the cache.
notes: The missing PERSISTENT anti-ant engine, giving ants the per-threat engine answer that mould (Melanized Sheath) and worms (Arthrobotrys Snare) already have. Buy 8, repay 3 via recovered pile energy/drafts on ant-heavy maps. Defense/utility engine, no energy output, exempt from energy ceiling. Dead-ish on ant-light maps = the timing/opportunity read.

name: Trail Hijack
effect: One-shot. Choose one ant trail your network touches: convert it into a conductive cord — instantly extend your frontier along its full length AND gain +12 energy from the forage the ants had cached on it. If no ant trail is touched, the card is wasted.
flavor: Repurposing the ants' pheromone highway as your own pre-built rhizomorph.
notes: Turns the ant race into upside, mirroring the worm->N profit loop. Net positive only when an ant trail blocks/touches you, so it's situational not auto-include. +12 energy roughly refunds buy + a draw; the free extension is the real value (skips a dig). Provides a route/trail-clearing function ants lacked.

name: Mycoparasitic Coil
effect: Install. Each round, if a Trichoderma cloud is within sight of your frontier, coil around and digest one cloud cell: remove it and gain +1 Nitrogen. If no cloud is in sight, produces nothing.
flavor: You parasitize the parasite: chitinase-tipped coils constricting Trichoderma itself.
notes: Gives mould a resource-upside loop like worms->N (and references real Trichoderma mycoparasitism turned back on it). Uncommon buy 16, repay 4 in-band when mould is present (clears clouds + N). Conditional output is the timing read: dead on mould-light maps. Resource/defense engine, exempt from energy ceiling.

name: Laccase Curtain
effect: Install. Each round, oxidatively detoxify one strand cluster: grant it 2-round mould immunity AND repair 1 rotted cell. Produces no energy.
flavor: A rolling laccase curtain oxidizing Trichoderma toxins before they bind.
notes: Fills the empty mid-tier mould ENGINE slot between common Melanized Sheath and reactive mould events. Distinct from Laccase Cascade (digestion-efficiency engine) and from Mycoparasitic Coil (this is defensive immunity+repair, not N production). Defense engine, exempt from energy ceiling. Repay 4 via rot prevented; trap if bought on mould-free maps.

name: Apatite Detonation
effect: One-shot. Spend 4 Phosphorus: shatter an entire rock COLUMN or mineral formation barrier in front of you, opening a wide multi-row breach, then collect +6 Phosphorus of scattered debris.
flavor: Concentrated oxalic acid loaded into one fracture plane until the column splits.
notes: The marquee pure-P 4-resource sink, matching Monsoon Bloom (4W) and Aerial Spore Cast/GS-GOGAT (N). Net P cost is -4 then +6 = +2 P refund, so it's a column-removal payoff that nearly pays its own resource back — the gate is amassing 4 P first (the 'save it, harvest more' tension) plus the 28 buy. Late-timing: a column-skip swing right before the final dig.

name: Translocation Cord
effect: Install. Once per 3 rounds: convert 2 of any one resource (W/P/N) into 2 of another (W/P/N). Cannot net-create resources beyond the 2-for-2 swap.
flavor: Cytoplasmic streaming hauling solutes the length of the cord to where they're needed.
notes: The missing resource converter. With lakeCountMax=1, Water can be unreachable and W-gated power cards go dead; this rebalances across the orthogonal resources without hoarding (1-for-1 value at 2-for-2 nominal, capped, cooldown-limited). Action install, repay 0 (no per-round value). Opportunity cost: a worse fit than the right harvest route when you have it.

name: Decay Foray
effect: Add 4 'Scavenge' basics to your draw deck, each of which produces +1 Nitrogen when played. Then this card goes to the discard (not recycled).
flavor: Foraging runners fanning across the leaf-mould for nitrogen-rich scraps.
notes: The missing N-basic EXTENDER, parity with Capillary Runners (W), Polyphosphate Granule (P), and Hyphal Tip Extension / Mycelial Fan-Out (Grow). Adds runway (4 cards) AND a steady N drip you must spend energy to draw. Extender goes to graveyard per invariant 4. Early timing — adding runway late wastes most of the cards.

name: Foxfire Glow
effect: One-shot. Bioluminesce: reveal all map features (food piles, lakes, formations, rock columns, threat nests) within a wide radius of your frontier, and mark the lowest-cost route to the nearest unrevealed food pile.
flavor: Luciferin-driven foxfire glow lighting the dark tunnels (Armillaria, Mycena, Omphalotus).
notes: Fills the under-served routing/scouting axis with real biology (bioluminescent wood-rot fungi). Value is highest EARLY when the route is unknown; near-dead LATE once the map is explored = the timing read. Cheap common one-shot, no resource gate. No existing card does pure feature reveal/route-planning.

name: Spitzenkorper Focus
effect: Install. Once per 2 rounds: concentrate the apical vesicle body to drive one long, straight forward extension (3x a normal Grow's reach) in a single chosen direction. No turns mid-extension.
flavor: The Spitzenkorper — the vesicle supply center at the hyphal apex that aims all tip growth.
notes: Teaches the single most iconic structure of fungal tip growth, absent from the pool. Repeatable burst-traversal action (distinct from one-shot Cord Surge/Enzymatic Deep Bore and from per-round growth engines). The straight-only constraint is the opportunity cost — great on open runs, awkward around columns. Action install, repay 0.

name: Demarcation Line
effect: Install. Each round, extend a melanized zone line one cell along the boundary where your network meets a threat colony (ant trail OR mould cloud), blocking that threat's spread across the line. Produces no energy.
flavor: Somatic incompatibility: where two colonies reject each other a black zone line forms.
notes: Uses the striking real phenomenon of melanized zone lines (somatic incompatibility), unused in the pool. Flexible cheap defense engine vs both ants and mould (threat:all), repay 3 on contested maps. Defense engine, exempt from energy ceiling. Weaker than a dedicated single-threat engine on a mono-threat map = the draft tension.

name: Chlamydospore Bank
effect: Install. Each round, bank +2 energy into thick-walled spores instead of spending it; the bank holds up to 20. While card-dry, you may release the bank (any round) for the stored energy at no skip cost. Per-round banking counts toward the engine energy ceiling.
flavor: Chlamydospores — thick-walled asexual survival spores distinct from sclerotia.
notes: Diversifies the survival/insurance family away from over-used sclerotia. The +2/round energy is real income so it COUNTS toward the sum<12 ceiling (invariant 1, 5): stacking it with two big energy engines breaks the cap — deliberate trade-off, not a violation. The 20-cap release is endgame runway, not a reshuffle. Repay 3, early.

name: Autophagic Sprint
effect: One-shot. Cannibalize older hyphae for a burst: gain +24 energy now, but PERMANENTLY raise your SKIP cost by 2 for the rest of the level (this never lowers SKIP below the base floor — only raises it).
flavor: Autophagy: recycling your own cytoplasm into a forward sprint at lasting cost.
notes: A genuine risk/reward card with a real downside (deepens opportunity cost; pool is almost all upside). +24 now vs a steeper end-of-level bleed. Strongest EARLY (you'll skip few times after) — playing it late when you'll skip a lot is a trap = the timing read. Explicitly states SKIP only goes UP, so it can't interact with skip-reducer floors to break invariant 5.

name: Hymenial Surge Bed
effect: Install. Each round, lay down spore-bearing hymenium: +3 spores toward your final fruiting yield AND +1 of a resource of your choice (W/P/N). Produces no energy.
flavor: The hymenium — the fertile spore-producing tissue lining the maturing fruit body.
notes: Fills the empty 'late engine that breaks even in ~2 rounds' band the timingTiers spec allows but the pool never populated. Repay 2 measured in spore/final-yield value (3 spores/round high-value near the goal). Resource output exempt from energy ceiling. Buying it EARLY is a trap — spores only matter near fruiting, so it's a late-only payoff engine, the inverse of Saprotrophic Mat's 'too late' lesson.

name: Cordyceps Vault
effect: Install. Each round, +4 energy from deep stromatic reserves. No resource gate. Counts toward the engine energy ceiling.
flavor: A dense stroma quietly metabolizing buried substrate at maximum sustainable rate.
notes: The marquee EARLY high-buy(28) NO-gate engine whose tension is purely energy-banking ('great but bank 28 first, turn 1 you can't afford it after starting moves'). Repay 6 = in-band for rare but ONLY if played early; the longest-repay engine in the pool, so it is unambiguously WRONG to buy late = teaches 'too late to repay' on the energy axis. +4/round is the per-engine max; with sum<12 ceiling it crowds out other energy engines (invariant 1/5) = real trade-off.
